title: The Art of War: thirteen chapters in six steps

modules.title: Laying plans
modules.summary: War is a vital matter of state that requires careful deliberation through five constant factors, deceptive tactics, and thorough planning before any battle is fought.

lessons.title: The five constant factors
lessons.explainer: Sun Tzu explains that the art of war is a matter of life and death for the state, governed by five constant factors. A student learns that military planning begins with fundamental conditions like the Moral Law, which aligns the people completely with their ruler.

key_terms.meaning: Causes the people to be in complete accord with their ruler.

lessons.title: Heaven, Earth and the Commander
lessons.explainer: This section defines the remaining constant factors: Heaven, Earth, the Commander, and Method and discipline. Students learn that a general must be familiar with all five heads to achieve victory rather than failure.

key_terms.meaning: Signifies night and day, cold and heat, times and seasons.
Comprises distances, danger, security, open ground, and narrow passes.

lessons.title: All warfare is deception
lessons.explainer: Warfare is fundamentally based on deception, requiring generals to hide their true strength and use baits to entice the enemy. Students see that victory belongs to the commander who makes many calculations in advance.

key_terms.meaning: The foundational principle upon which all warfare is based.

quiz.question: What does Sun Tzu state that the art of war is governed by?
options: Three elemental forces
Five constant factors
Ten tactical principles
Four seasons of combat
quiz.explanation: The art of war, then, is governed by five constant factors, to be taken into account in one's deliberations.
quiz.support: The art of war, then, is governed by five constant factors, to be taken into account in one’s deliberations, when seeking to determine the conditions obtaining in the field.

quiz.question: What is all warfare based on according to Sun Tzu?
options: Superior numbers
Strict discipline
Deception
Financial resources
quiz.explanation: All warfare is based on deception.
quiz.support: All warfare is based on deception.

quiz.question: What does a general who wins a battle do beforehand in his temple?
options: Makes many calculations
Prays for divine favor
Sacrifices white horses
Gathers all his officers
quiz.explanation: Now the general who wins a battle makes many calculations in his temple ere the battle is fought.
quiz.support: Now the general who wins a battle makes many calculations in his temple ere the battle is fought.

modules.title: The cost of war
modules.summary: Campaigns are extremely costly and should be short, as prolonged warfare exhausts the state's resources and invites outside threats.

lessons.title: What a campaign costs
lessons.explainer: Maintaining an army in the field demands enormous financial and material expenditures every single day. A student understands that long sieges and delayed victories quickly exhaust an army's strength and dull its weapons.

key_terms.meaning: Vehicles used in operations of war alongside mail-clad soldiers.

lessons.title: No profit in a long war
lessons.explainer: Protracted campaigns drain state resources and invite other chieftains to attack a weakened nation. Students learn that long delays in war have never benefited any country.

key_terms.meaning: A long campaign that strains the resources of the State.

lessons.title: Using the enemy's strength
lessons.explainer: Clever leaders augment their own strength by capturing enemy resources and treating prisoners kindly. For a student, this highlights that the ultimate goal of war is swift victory rather than lengthy campaigns.

key_terms.meaning: The leader of armies upon whom the nation's fate depends.

quiz.question: What happens when a campaign is protracted and resources are strained?
options: The enemy surrenders out of exhaustion
Other chieftains will spring up to take advantage of your extremity
The ruler must abdicate the throne
New alliances will be formed with neighbors
quiz.explanation: Now, when your weapons are dulled, your ardour damped, your strength exhausted and your treasure spent, other chieftains will spring up to take advantage of your extremity.
quiz.support: Now, when your weapons are dulled, your ardour damped, your strength exhausted and your treasure spent, other chieftains will spring up to take advantage of your extremity.

quiz.question: According to Sun Tzu, has a country ever benefited from prolonged warfare?
options: Yes, if the victory is absolute
Only when the treasury is full
There is no instance of it
Yes, after initial heavy losses
quiz.explanation: There is no instance of a country having benefited from prolonged warfare.
quiz.support: There is no instance of a country having benefited from prolonged warfare.

quiz.question: How should captured soldiers be treated in chariot fighting?
options: They should be kindly treated and kept
They should be returned to their commanders
They should be set free immediately
They should be put to work on the roads
quiz.explanation: The captured soldiers should be kindly treated and kept.
quiz.support: The captured soldiers should be kindly treated and kept.

quiz.question: In war, what should your great object be?
options: Territorial expansion
Victory, not lengthy campaigns
The total destruction of the enemy
Gaining the respect of other rulers
quiz.explanation: In war, then, let your great object be victory, not lengthy campaigns.
quiz.support: In war, then, let your great object be victory, not lengthy campaigns.

modules.title: Winning without fighting
modules.summary: The highest form of generalship is to conquer the enemy without fighting by knowing both yourself and your opponent thoroughly.

lessons.title: Take it whole
lessons.explainer: The supreme excellence in war is breaking the enemy's resistance without fighting by taking states and armies whole. Students learn that baulking enemy plans is far superior to besieging walled cities.

key_terms.meaning: The skill of leading an army, with its highest form aiming to baulk enemy plans.

lessons.title: Avoid sieges; the ruler's errors
lessons.explainer: Sieges waste months and cost many lives through frustrated assaults. Students learn that rulers can bring misfortune upon their armies by interfering with commands or ignoring military conditions.

key_terms.meaning: A term describing the general as the defense of the State.

lessons.title: Know the enemy and yourself
lessons.explainer: Victory relies on five key points, culminating in the famous rule to know both the enemy and yourself. A student learns that mutual knowledge prevents failure across a hundred battles.

key_terms.meaning: The opposing force that one must know alongside oneself.

quiz.question: In the practical art of war, what is the best thing of all to do?
options: To take the enemy's country whole and intact
To destroy the enemy's capital city
To kill the enemy commander in single combat
To capture all their weapons and supplies
quiz.explanation: In the practical art of war, the best thing of all is to take the enemy's country whole and intact; to shatter and destroy it is not so good.
quiz.support: Sun Tzŭ said: In the practical art of war, the best thing of all is to take the enemy’s country whole and intact; to shatter and destroy it is not so good.

quiz.question: What constitutes supreme excellence in the art of war?
options: Winning a hundred battles in a row
Conquering all neighboring states
Breaking the enemy's resistance without fighting
Starving the enemy out of their walled cities
quiz.explanation: ...supreme excellence consists in breaking the enemy's resistance without fighting.
quiz.support: Hence to fight and conquer in all your battles is not supreme excellence; supreme excellence consists in breaking the enemy’s resistance without fighting.

quiz.question: What is it called when a ruler commands the army to advance or retreat while ignorant that it cannot obey?
options: Hobbling the army
Undermining the state
Flinging victory away
Spreading anarchy
quiz.explanation: This is called hobbling the army.
quiz.support: This is called hobbling the army.

modules.title: Position and energy
modules.summary: Good fighters secure themselves against defeat first, using indirect methods and arriving early in the field to impose their will.

lessons.title: Beyond the possibility of defeat
lessons.explainer: Good fighters first establish their own invincibility through defensive tactics before waiting for enemy mistakes. Students learn that security is in one's own hands, while victory opportunities are provided by the opponent.

key_terms.meaning: Tactics that secure a force against defeat.

lessons.title: Direct and indirect
lessons.explainer: While direct methods join battle, indirect tactics are essential for securing victory and offer endless combinations. Students see that these tactics resemble the inexhaustible flow of rivers or the four seasons.

key_terms.meaning: A method used for joining battle.

lessons.title: First in the field
lessons.explainer: The army that arrives first in the field rests and forces its will upon the exhausted latecomers. Students learn that a clever combatant controls the enemy through advantages, harassment, or starvation.

key_terms.meaning: A fighter who imposes his will on the enemy.

quiz.question: What did the good fighters of old do first?
options: Gathered intelligence on enemy leaders
Put themselves beyond the possibility of defeat
Secured abundant provisions for the march
Trained their soldiers in chariot combat
quiz.explanation: The good fighters of old first put themselves beyond the possibility of defeat, and then waited for an opportunity of defeating the enemy.
quiz.support: Sun Tzŭ said: The good fighters of old first put themselves beyond the possibility of defeat, and then waited for an opportunity of defeating the enemy.

quiz.question: How does Sun Tzu describe the inexhaustibility of efficiently applied indirect tactics?
options: Like gold and silver in a royal treasury
As Heaven and Earth, unending as the flow of rivers and streams
Like the trees in a vast mountain forest
As the number of stars in the night sky
quiz.explanation: Indirect tactics, efficiently applied, are inexhaustible as Heaven and Earth, unending as the flow of rivers and streams...
quiz.support: Indirect tactics, efficiently applied, are inexhaustible as Heaven and Earth, unending as the flow of rivers and streams; like the sun and moon, they end but to begin anew; like the four seasons, they pass away but to return once more.

quiz.question: What advantage does whoever is first in the field enjoy?
options: They can choose the weather for the battle
They will be fresh for the fight
They can capture the enemy's baggage train
They will have the support of local guides
quiz.explanation: Whoever is first in the field and awaits the coming of the enemy, will be fresh for the fight...
quiz.support: Sun Tzŭ said: Whoever is first in the field and awaits the coming of the enemy, will be fresh for the fight; whoever is second in the field and has to hasten to battle, will arrive exhausted.

modules.title: Manoeuvre and ground
modules.summary: A general must adapt to different kinds of terrain, move only for real advantage, and maintain the welfare and discipline of the soldiers.

lessons.title: Move only for advantage
lessons.explainer: Commanders must use local guides, practice dissimulation, and move only when there is real advantage. Students learn to make their movements as swift as wind and as dark as night.

key_terms.meaning: A practice in war essential for success.

lessons.title: Six kinds of terrain
lessons.explainer: Sun Tzu categorizes terrain into six distinct types that dictate tactical movement and survival. Students learn that failing to understand specific terrains like entangling ground leads directly to disaster.

key_terms.meaning: Different kinds of ground encountered in the field.

lessons.title: The general and the ruler
lessons.explainer: A true general fights when victory is certain regardless of a ruler's commands, seeking neither fame nor disgrace. Students see that soldiers treated like beloved children will stand by their leader unto death.

key_terms.meaning: A description of the selfless general who protects his country.

quiz.question: What must be used if natural advantages are to be turned to account?
options: Local guides
Surviving spies
Chariot divisions
Captured officers
quiz.explanation: We shall be unable to turn natural advantages to account unless we make use of local guides.
quiz.support: We shall be unable to turn natural advantages to account unless we make use of local guides.

quiz.question: What is the definition of entangling ground?
options: Ground which can be abandoned but is hard to re-occupy
Ground surrounded on all sides by narrow passes
Ground that is situated at a great distance from the enemy
Ground where neither side can maneuver chariots
quiz.explanation: Ground which can be abandoned but is hard to re-occupy is called entangling.
quiz.support: Ground which can be abandoned but is hard to re-occupy is called _entangling_.

quiz.question: What should a general do if fighting is sure to result in victory?
options: Ask the ruler for formal permission
Wait until supplies are doubled
Fight, even though the ruler forbid it
Consult the local guides first
quiz.explanation: If fighting is sure to result in victory, then you must fight, even though the ruler forbid it...
quiz.support: If fighting is sure to result in victory, then you must fight, even though the ruler forbid it; if fighting will not result in victory, then you must not fight even at the ruler’s bidding.

modules.title: Fire and foreknowledge
modules.summary: Wars should never be fought out of anger, and gaining crucial foreknowledge depends entirely on employing five types of spies.

lessons.title: Move not unless you see an advantage
lessons.explainer: Enlightened rulers plan ahead and never engage in war out of anger or pique. Students learn that destroyed kingdoms and dead lives can never be brought back.

key_terms.meaning: A description of the ruler who lays plans well ahead.

lessons.title: Foreknowledge
lessons.explainer: Because war is intensely costly, grudging money for spies is the height of inhumanity. Students learn that vital foreknowledge cannot be gained from spirits or deduction, but only from men.

key_terms.meaning: What enables the wise sovereign and good general to conquer.

lessons.title: Five kinds of spies
lessons.explainer: Sun Tzu outlines five distinct classes of spies—local, inward, converted, doomed, and surviving—who form a secret system. Students learn that spies require the closest relations, liberal rewards, and absolute secrecy.

key_terms.meaning: Agents used to obtain knowledge of the enemy's dispositions.

quiz.question: What does the enlightened ruler do according to the chapter on fire?
options: Lays his plans well ahead
Consults the spirits for foreknowledge
Leads the vanguard into battle personally
Rewards the surviving spies liberally
quiz.explanation: The enlightened ruler lays his plans well ahead; the good general cultivates his resources.
quiz.support: Hence the saying: The enlightened ruler lays his plans well ahead; the good general cultivates his resources.

quiz.question: Why is remaining in ignorance of the enemy's condition by grudging money for spies considered the height of inhumanity?
options: Because spies are cheap to employ
Because a single day decides a victory while armies face each other for years
Because it leads directly to the destruction of the ruler's palace
Because soldiers will mutiny if they lack intelligence
quiz.explanation: Hostile armies may face each other for years, striving for the victory which is decided in a single day. This being so, to remain in ignorance... is the height of inhumanity.
quiz.support: Hostile armies may face each other for years, striving for the victory which is decided in a single day.

quiz.question: With whom in the whole army should the most intimate relations be maintained?
options: The senior generals
Spies
Local guides
The royal ministers
quiz.explanation: Hence it is that with none in the whole army are more intimate relations to be maintained than with spies.
quiz.support: Having _inward spies_, making use of officials of the enemy.
